_purpose: Reference library for building detailed, structured AI image/video prompts. Distilled from AI Video Bootcamp course materials (camera movement catalogue, camera-as-language guide, color grading reference, contrast/realism trick guide, AI video generation settings guide) plus a large sample of professional-grade prompt examples. Used to ground the /episode Gemini prompt so scene prompts are structured and specific instead of one-liners.

image_prompt_anatomy.description: A strong image prompt is a short paragraph, not a single sentence. Build it from these components in roughly this order, only including what's relevant to the scene:
components: Subject and action: who/what, doing what, in one clear beat (one action, not several stacked together)
Camera position and shot size: angle (eye-level/low/high/dutch/frontal/three-quarter/profile/over-the-shoulder/POV) + shot size (extreme wide/wide/full/medium/close-up/extreme close-up)
Lens and depth of field: focal length in mm and what it does to the space, aperture (f-stop) and what stays sharp vs blurred
Lighting: direction, quality (hard/soft), source (window, practical lamp, overcast sky, neon, firelight), and what it does to the subject
Texture and realism detail: skin pores, fabric weave, imperfections, sweat/moisture, wear on props/clothing — concrete physical detail beats generic adjectives
Environment and background layers: foreground / midground / background described separately when the scene has depth
Camera/format reference: a real camera body or film stock when it helps set the character (see camera_bodies below)
Color grading: one mood-to-palette formula (see color_grading below), placed near the end
Composition note: what the frame emphasizes, where the subject sits (rule of thirds, centered, negative space)
Quality tag: photorealistic / cinematic / 8k / ultra-detailed — one short tag, not a paragraph
image_prompt_anatomy.rule: Prefer concrete, specific physical detail over generic superlatives. 'visible pores, a thin scar at the hairline, faint sunburn across the shoulders' beats 'flawless beautiful skin'. One clear subject action beats several stacked actions.

video_prompt_anatomy.description: A video prompt describes MOTION on top of the image, using the six-slot camera movement template. Keep it to ONE main subject movement and ONE main camera movement per scene — stacking multiple movements causes AI video models to glitch or morph.

six_slot_template.movement: The move by name and what it rides on (rails, shoulder, crane, drone, fixed tripod).
six_slot_template.start: How it begins — locked frame, or already moving on frame one.
six_slot_template.speed: The curve — ease in, build, decelerate, constant, violent, or creeping.
six_slot_template.framing: What stays stable while everything else changes (camera height, subject centering, horizon level).
six_slot_template.end: The final frame and the hold, or an exit still in motion.
six_slot_template.time: Real time, normal speed, no slow motion — unless the scene specifically calls for a time effect (freeze/bullet-time).

video_prompt_anatomy.rule: Never leave a decision to the model. Name the exact movement, its start state, its speed curve, what stays fixed, and how it ends. Do not just say 'slow push-in' — that names only the pace.

camera_movements.name: Static Shot
camera_movements.use_it: a face about to break, two people at a table, clean cut into next shot

camera_movements.name: Pan
camera_movements.use_it: follow someone crossing a room, carry attention from one thing to another

camera_movements.name: Tilt
camera_movements.use_it: introduce a character in pieces, boots to face

camera_movements.name: Whip Pan
camera_movements.use_it: reactions, reveals, comedic beats, invisible transitions

camera_movements.name: Dolly In
camera_movements.use_it: the moment something changes inside a person: a realization, a decision

camera_movements.name: Dolly Out
camera_movements.use_it: isolation, endings, and the reveal of what else is in the room

camera_movements.name: Zoom In / Out
camera_movements.use_it: tighten the frame without moving the audience through space

camera_movements.name: Slow Zoom
camera_movements.use_it: monologues, dread, a slow realization

camera_movements.name: Fast Zoom
camera_movements.use_it: a sudden discovery, a reality check

camera_movements.name: Crash Zoom In
camera_movements.use_it: comedic beats, sudden overwhelming realizations

camera_movements.name: Crash Zoom Out
camera_movements.use_it: comedy or shock: reveal the full context around a calm face

camera_movements.name: Truck
camera_movements.use_it: unfold a space piece by piece, the environment is the subject

camera_movements.name: Slider
camera_movements.use_it: tabletops, interiors, product shots, subtle foreground parallax

camera_movements.name: Pedestal
camera_movements.use_it: rise from evidence on a desk to the face reading it

camera_movements.name: Push Past
camera_movements.use_it: enter a scene through a doorframe/foreground object instead of cutting in

camera_movements.name: Arc
camera_movements.use_it: reveal another person or angle entering the frame, a quarter/half turn

camera_movements.name: Orbit
camera_movements.use_it: the whole world around the subject is worth showing; end on something new

camera_movements.name: Spiral
camera_movements.use_it: circling that closes toward one destination — obsession or release

camera_movements.name: Follow From Behind
camera_movements.use_it: walking into the unknown — a corridor, a crowd, a door ahead

camera_movements.name: Reverse Tracking
camera_movements.use_it: determination — someone who has decided and is on the way

camera_movements.name: Side Tracking
camera_movements.use_it: journeys, athletes, distance-covered montage beats

camera_movements.name: Low Tracking Shot
camera_movements.use_it: introductions that keep mystery, face never shown

camera_movements.name: Vehicle Tracking
camera_movements.use_it: when speed itself is the story — the escape, the chase

camera_movements.name: Chase Shot
camera_movements.use_it: panic, escape, pursuit — framing slips and corrects

camera_movements.name: Handheld Shot
camera_movements.use_it: scenes that should feel witnessed: arguments, horror, raw moments

camera_movements.name: Reactive Snap Zoom
camera_movements.use_it: action bursting into frame, or a comedic snap onto a face

camera_movements.name: Snorricam
camera_movements.use_it: panic, drunkenness, a mind coming apart — world spins around a locked face

camera_movements.name: Crane Up / Down
camera_movements.use_it: endings, openings, a life meeting the scale of the world

camera_movements.name: Drone Shot
camera_movements.use_it: geography and scale, where this story lives

camera_movements.name: Fly-Through
camera_movements.use_it: connect outside and inside through one opening, no cut

camera_movements.name: FPV Dive
camera_movements.use_it: adrenaline — the drop, the pursuit

camera_movements.name: Dolly Zoom
camera_movements.use_it: the moment reality shifts — the diagnosis, the betrayal

camera_movements.name: Bullet Time
camera_movements.use_it: the one decisive frozen instant — impact, leap, collision

shot_sizes.reads: the environment becomes the real subject

color_grading.formula: [scene description] + [lighting source] + [one color grade mood] + [film reference if useful] — placed near the end of the prompt. Never say just 'colorful'; name the exact colors. Pick one mood, not several stacked together.

moods.palette: rich golds, deep blues, warm highlights, cool shadows
desaturated, heavy shadows, teal and orange undertones
soft pinks, warm gold tones, slight haze
cold greens, sickly yellows, high contrast, crushed blacks
neon blues and magentas against dark backgrounds
faded colors, warm yellows, lifted blacks, film grain
bright, slightly cool, high key, minimal shadows
rich greens, warm earth tones, natural saturation
desaturated blue-grey, cold tones, overcast feel
high contrast, punchy saturation, warm with cool accents
deep blacks, gold accents, warm highlights, rich contrast
unnatural color shifts, pastels mixed with deep tones

film_references: Blade Runner 2049: heavy orange and teal, smoky atmosphere, neon in darkness
Mad Max: Fury Road: crushed teal shadows, blazing orange/amber highlights, extreme contrast
The Matrix: green tint throughout, dark shadows, desaturated except green
Wes Anderson: pastel color blocking, symmetrical, warm vintage tones
Ozark / Gone Girl: cold steel blue, desaturated, flat, oppressive
John Wick: deep neon blue and red against pitch black, high contrast
Dune: warm amber and sand tones, hazy atmosphere, desaturated blues
The Revenant: cold natural light, blue-grey shadows, raw and earthy

realism_notes: AI footage defaults to looking too clean: too much contrast, too saturated, too stable. For grounded/realistic (non-glossy) scenes, describe softer natural light, natural skin texture with visible pores/imperfections, and avoid words like 'flawless' or 'perfect'.
One main subject movement and one main camera movement per scene is the ceiling — stacked motion breaks AI video models.
Real, concrete physical detail (a scar, sweat, fabric wear, a stray hair) reads as more realistic than piled-on generic beauty adjectives.
Never invent a video/image model — only recommend models that appear in the routing table.
